item.title: Diri urges Bayelsa governorship aspirants to seek God
item.description: By Samuel Oyadongha, Yenagoa YENAGOA — Governor Douye Diri of Bayelsa State has urged anyone aspiring to succeed him to seek God’s approval through prayer, saying the next governor must be a God-fearing person. Diri spoke on Monday during the state’s 15th Thanksgiving service at the Ecumenical Centre, Igbogene, Yenagoa, where he declared that Bayelsa had been handed over to God. He said nobody could stop anyone chosen by God to lead the state, adding that the Almighty would always have the final say in its affairs. The governor also urged residents to remain united, tolerant and peaceful, describing these as essential conditions for the state’s development. He reaffirmed his administration’s commitment to improving the lives of residents, saying it had the political will to transform Bayelsa, which he described as one of the states with the best environments for development. Diri thanked the people for their support over the past six years and urged them to sustain their cooperation with the government. “All who want to be governor, go and seek the face of God. Anyone who wants to be governor must be God-fearing. If God said yes, nobody can say no, not even me,” he said. He added: “Let us continue to worship God. Let us be tolerant and patient as we will become victorious at the end of the day. “As I keep saying, those of us who were born in Yenagoa or know Bayelsa of old can see the difference today. It is enough to give thanks. “We have one of the best environments in Nigeria, and with the political will, we are bringing development to our people.” In his sermon, the guest preacher and former Bayelsa State Chairman of the Christian Association of Nigeria, Very Rev. Joseph Opelema, urged Christians to combine their religious faith with responsible citizenship. Speaking on the theme, “Called to be Good Christians and Good Citizens,” Opelema said Christians had dual responsibilities as members of the church and citizens of society. Drawing his message from Matthew 22:15-22, where Jesus addressed the question of paying taxes, he said the biblical instruction to give to Caesar what belongs to Caesar and to God what belongs to God underscored the importance of responsible citizenship. The cleric said Christians should demonstrate sacrifice, prudence, accountability, justice, love, care and charity wherever they found themselves, particularly in public office. He lamented what he described as a gap between religious participation and the practice of Christian values, urging believers to become witnesses, the salt of the earth and the light of the world. Opelema also described Bayelsa as richly endowed with natural and human resources, favourable weather, land and rivers, which he said could make the state a tourism destination. He expressed optimism that the state could realise its potential with God-fearing leadership. item.title: North Korea slams FBI allegations over Binance hack as ‘grave’ provocation
item.description: North Korea on Tuesday slammed the FBI’s allegations that Pyongyang was behind the theft of $6 billion from cryptocurrency platform Binance, with Kim Jong Un’s powerful sister labelling it a “grave political provocation”. Kim Yo Jong, in a statement released Tuesday by the KCNA state news agency, said the FBI’s claim was “absurd rhetoric and nothing new,” given prior US allegations that North Korea was behind last year’s major hack of Bybit. “It is a grave political provocation against the DPRK that the US misleads the international public opinion as if all the cyber crimes in different parts of the world are our deeds,” Kim said, using the acronym for North Korea’s official name. The FBI said on Saturday that a North Korea-affiliated hacking group called TraderTraitor had been behind the hack. TraderTraitor is the same group blamed for a $1.5 billion theft from the Bybit platform in February last year, which had been the largest crypto theft until the Binance hack. “This is a sinister attempt to damage the international image of the DPRK and undermine its dignity and national prestige and another grave violation of the sovereignty of the DPRK,” Kim said. “It is the consistent policy stand of the DPRK government to resolutely oppose all sorts of malicious acts in cyberspace,” she added. Binance is the world’s largest crypto exchange by daily trading volumes. News of the hacking attack caused the prices of most major cryptocurrencies to fall sharply on Friday. After the FBI released its statement on Saturday, US President Donald Trump cast doubt on North Korea’s involvement in the hack. “I’m not concerned. We’re learning about it. We don’t know if it’s North Korea,” Trump told reporters at his residence in Florida. Trump has made repeated overtures to nuclear-armed North Korea since returning to office, and said he was open to meeting with supreme leader Kim Jong Un this year. Those gestures have been met with silence from Pyongyang. Kim Yo Jong, in her statement, said the new allegations “confirmed Washington’s hostile attitude toward the DPRK once again.” “We have issues to reconsider in diverse aspects as regards the very unpleasant US hostile attitude,” she added. item.title: Critics of Rainbow Coalition can’t unite their families – Wike
item.description: By Omeiza Ajayi – ABUJA Minister of the Federal Capital Territory FCT, Nyesom Wike, has said politicians who deny the existence of the Rainbow Coalition lack the capacity to unite even their own families and communities. Read Also: 2027: Obi couldn’t fix Anambra; Atiku will return to Dubai after election — Oshiomhole Wike spoke on Monday in Abuja at the commissioning of the Gwagwalada Civic Centre and an interactive session with stakeholders of the All Progressives Congress APC and the Peoples Democratic Party PDP in Gwagwalada Area Council. The minister said the coalition, which brings together political stakeholders from both parties, was formed in the interest of unity, cooperation and development in the FCT. “Some greedy and selfish politicians do not understand what we call unity. They have no capacity to hold their space, they have no capacity to even hold their families, and they have no capacity to hold their communities. So they can open their mouths and say there is no Rainbow Coalition,” he said. Wike challenged critics of the alliance to explain why political leaders who once disagreed could not come together to pursue common interests. He described the development in Gwagwalada as a departure from the politics of confrontation, insisting that the FCT needed cooperation rather than needless political hostility. Commending political leaders in the area for setting aside their differences, he said their decision showed that the collective interest of the people outweighed individual political ambition. Wike also urged residents not to repeat what he described as the mistake of the 2023 general elections, and called for credible representation at the National Assembly. The minister canvassed support for a former senator, Philip Aduda, and other candidates endorsed by the coalition, saying political representatives must be accessible and familiar with their constituents. Wike also declared support for the re-election of President Bola Tinubu and urged residents to turn their endorsements into votes in 2027. “On the day of the election, it will not be a day for market or fishing. It is the day all of us have decided to come together and demonstrate our strength through our votes. Go to the polling units, districts and communities and mobilise the people to vote for Bola Ahmed Tinubu,” he said. APC chair Earlier, the FCT APC Chairman, Ishaku Tanko Yamawo, described the gathering as historic, saying Wike’s intervention had brought together leaders who previously operated on opposing sides. The FCT PDP Chairman, Alhaji Ismaila Mohammed Dogara, praised Wike for his development interventions, particularly the revival of a project abandoned for 16 years in Gwagwalada. The Aguma of Gwagwalada, Alhaji Muhammadu Magaji, also commended Wike’s contributions to the development of the territory. item.title: EPL: Everton deepen Newcastle crisis with 1-0 win
item.description: Everton increased the pressure on under-fire Newcastle boss Matthias Jaissle as Thierno Barry sealed a 1-0 win at St James’ Park on Monday. Barry netted early in the second half to lift Everton into seventh place in the Premier League and leave Newcastle languishing in 13th. Newcastle midfielder Jacob Ramsey was sent off in the final seconds for a crude foul on Harrison Armstrong. It was a fitting end to another painful defeat for Saudi-funded Newcastle, who have lost four of their past five matches in all competitions, winning just twice in their last seven. Jaissle and his players were booed off at half-time and again after the final whistle as the German coach begins to feel the heat in his first season in charge. Hired following Eddie Howe’s surprise close-season exit, former Red Bull Salzburg and Al-Ahli boss Jaissle has struggled to make an impact on Tyneside. Jaissle desperately needs a win at fellow strugglers Fulham on Saturday to ease the mounting scrutiny. Bizarrely, Newcastle have lost 22 of their last 33 Premier League matches on a Monday and many of their supporters headed for the exits well before the final whistle on a miserable rainy night. Barry’s eighth goal this season, including four in his last six matches, gave Everton their second win against Newcastle in the space of five days following their 3-1 victory in the League Cup fourth round on Thursday. Everton ended their run of two successive league defeats after losing against Arsenal and Chelsea. It was Everton’s first away league win since February 28 when they took three points on their previous visit to Newcastle. Jack Grealish was absent from the Everton squad for a second successive game after being axed for the Newcastle match last week due to a “breach of club discipline”. – Ramsey sees red – The on-loan Manchester City winger, who has been criticised for his off-field behaviour for much of his colourful career, reportedly skipped training prior to the League Cup clash. Everton said he was “not match fit” for the rematch with the Magpies, but his team coped just fine without him. Newcastle made a lively start and went close when Harvey Barnes fired just wide before Joelinton was narrowly off target from 25 yards. But chances were at a premium for both sides in a scrappy first half more notable for perspiration than inspiration. Everton’s opener four minutes after half-time was in keeping with the grimy fare that preceded it. Newcastle’s dismal marking let in Tyrique George for a shot that drew a weak save from Lukas Hornicek. Hornicek could only push it straight into the path of Barry for a simple tap-in that survived a lengthy VAR check for offside. It was a chance so easy that even the notoriously erratic Barry couldn’t fail to hit the target, although Newcastle were aggrieved by the VAR decision to let it stand. item.title: Tinubu fulfils WAFCON pledge, as Super Falcons players receive $100,000 each
item.description: The Federal Government has fulfilled President Bola Tinubu’s reward pledge to the Super Falcons following their historic 10th Women’s Africa Cup of Nations (WAFCON) title victory. The National Sports Commission (NSC) announced that the players, coaches and officials of the team had received their cash rewards in naira equivalent of $100,000 for each player and $50,000 for officials. The cash payments form part of the presidential reward package announced after the Super Falcons defeated their opponents to clinch their record-extending 10th WAFCON title. 𝙋𝙍𝙀𝙎𝙎 𝙍𝙀𝙇𝙀𝘼𝙎𝙀 The Federal Government, through the National Sports Commission (NSC), has fulfilled President @officialABAT Bola Ahmed Tinubu GCFR’s reward pledge to the Super Falcons @NGSuper_Falcons , with players, coaches and officials receiving their cash awards… pic.twitter.com/eGRfmA40HP — National Sports Commission (@NatSportsComm) November 2, 2026 In addition to the cash rewards, each of the players and officials had earlier received a three-bedroom flat in Abuja and the national honour of Officer of the Order of the Niger (OON). The commission celebrated the fulfilment of the presidential pledge, describing the timely disbursement of the rewards as recognition of the team’s contribution to Nigerian sports. Nigeria secured its 10th WAFCON title in July 2025 after defeating hosts Morocco 3-2 in the final, coming from two goals down to complete a remarkable comeback and maintain its dominance in African women’s football. The victory further extended the Super Falcons’ record as the most successful team in the history of the continental women’s competition. item.title: [VIDEO] Tinubu’s Aide Refutes Claim President Visited Saudi Arabia To Get Northern Votes
item.description: Senior Special Assistant to President Bola Tinubu on Foreign Affairs and Protocol, Ademola Oshodi, has dismissed claims that the President visited Mecca in Saudi Arabia to curry favour with northerners, ahead of the 2027 general elections. Oshodi, who stated this during an interview on Channels Television’s Politics Today on Monday, said the trip was strictly religious as the President is a Muslim. The aide said that Tinubu’s presence in Mecca was not political, adding that even an opposition governor, Bala Mohammed of Bauchi State, was also present as a Muslim. He advised other presidential candidates in the 2027 general elections to also seek favour from God. The presidential aide said that though Nigerians are going through hardship, Tinubu is working to make things better. The President arrived in Saudi Arabia on October 29 and performed the religious rites associated with Umrah, seeking Allah’s guidance and blessings for Nigeria and its people. After completing the rites, he said that he felt fulfilled. Tinubu, who is the All Progressives Congress (APC) presidential candidate in the 2027 general elections, also said that God has granted him the wisdom to continue to lead Nigerians. item.title: [VIDEO] Umrah: No Second Term Can Be Given To Anybody Via Spiritual Claim — Atiku’s Spokesperson
item.description: Director of Strategic Communication of the African Democratic Congress (ADC) Presidential Campaign Council, Phrank Shaibu, has criticised President Bola Tinubu’s trip to Saudi Arabia for Umrah, saying a second term in office cannot be guaranteed via a spiritual claim. The spokesperson for the ADC presidential candidate, Atiku Abubakar, stated this during an interview on Channels Television’s Politics Today on Monday. Shaibu said that visiting the holy land should be a personal affair and not national, accusing Tinubu’s supporters of politicising the event. ﻿ He questioned the President’s faith, saying former Kaduna State governor, Nasir El-Rufai, would not remain in custody if Tinubu had sincerity of faith. Shaibu also accused the President of speaking into a mic in Saudi Arabia while Nigerians “are dying of hunger”. He said that Tinubu administration’s claim that the economy has improved is false, as many Nigerians are facing hardship. According to him, Nigerians will remember Tinubu’s prayer in Mecca the same way they remember the high prices of food, goods and services. Asked whether Atiku would have accompanied Tinubu to Saudi Arabia if he had been invited, the aide said that the former vice president sponsored the President’s first trip to Mecca. On the chances of the ADC candidate in the 2027 presidential election across the northern states, Shaibu said Atiku is home and dry in the region. Tinubu departed Abuja for Makkah on October 29, where he performed the religious rites associated with Umrah, seeking Allah’s guidance and blessings for Nigeria and its people. Speaking shortly after completing the religious rites, which he described as a spiritual experience and an opportunity to pray for Nigeria, the President said he felt fulfilled. The All Progressives Congress (APC) presidential candidate in the 2027 general elections also said that God has granted him the wisdom to continue to lead Nigerians. “Well, I asked for wisdom and resilience to continue to serve the people. I know that has been granted. “Prior to the 2023 election, I did the same thing. I asked Allah to bless my Umrah then. He did, and I promised that I would come back to thank him, Almighty Allah. “There is no other God but him. He is the giver and the taker. “He owns the power. He said, ‘Use it well. If you don’t use it in accordance with my dictates, I can take it from you and give it to another person,’ Tinubu told journalists. “So, I have faith in that and believe extremely well that he has done me a favour to be the President of this great country.” The post [VIDEO] Umrah: No Second Term Can Be Given To Anybody Via Spiritual Claim — Atiku’s Spokesperson appeared first on Channels Television .

item.title: N1.3 billion worth of property saved from fire in Nasarawa
item.description: By Edwin Philip, Lafia Property worth N1.3 billion has been saved from destruction by fire in Nasarawa State, while assets valued at N2.1 billion were exposed to fire hazards. The incidents resulted in estimated property losses of N800 million and one recorded death. However, fire crews successfully rescued eight victims from life-threatening situations during the period. These figures were recorded across approximately 97 emergency calls received from January to date. This was revealed by the Nasarawa State Controller of Federal Fire Service (FFS) Commander of Fire, Eno Kelechi Nwachukwu, during the flag off ceremony of the 2026 National Fire Week Awareness Campaign, which took place on Monday at the Federal Secretariat Lafia, the Nasarawa State capital. In her opening speech, Nwachukwu reaffirms Fire Service commitment to maintaining rapid response capabilities, while urging residents, business owners, and market associations to prioritize fire safety precautions and report emergencies immediately to minimize casualties and property damage. She said ” Fire safety is not the responsibility of the Federal Fire Service alone, It is a collective responsibility that requires the active participation of government, private organizations, institutions, families, community leaders, and every individual”. Delivering this year’s address under the theme “Building a Fire Resilient Nigeria: One Community at a time, the State Controller of Federal Fire Service, highlighted the critical need to shift from reactive emergency responses to proactive, community-driven prevention strategies. Defining the vision of a fire-resilient nation, the State Controller described it as a state where families, schools, businesses, and industrial centers possess the awareness, capacity, and infrastructure needed to prevent disasters, respond effectively, and recover swiftly when emergencies occur. ​ The Fire Service chief warned against negligence, noting that fire disasters do not discriminate between government establishments, private residences, commercial markets, or places of worship. ​To mitigate risks, the Federal Fire Service announced an intensified public education drive focusing on common household and commercial hazards. ” Key priorities include educating community members on Safe handling and storage of Liquefied Petroleum Gas (LPG/cooking gas, ​prevention of illegal and improper electrical connection​Curbing the indiscriminate burning of refuse​Proper storage of petroleum products and combustible materials ​She stressed that the nation’s overall security and economic stability begin at the local level, urging residence of the State to embrace safety standards in their daily activities to protect years of hard work, investments, and human lives. item.title: INEC pledges inclusive voting for PwDs
item.description: The Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC) has pledged to strengthen electoral accessibility for persons with disabilities (PwDs) ahead of the 2027 general elections. The commission said it would provide assistive materials, improve polling unit accessibility and train electoral officials to ensure inclusive participation. Gombe State Resident Electoral Commissioner, Alhaji Umar Gajiram, gave the assurance on Monday during a sensitisation workshop in Gombe. Gajiram, represented by the Administrative Secretary, Hajiya Fadimatu Bakari, said every Nigerian deserved equal opportunities to participate in democratic processes. He stressed that disability should never prevent eligible citizens from exercising their constitutional voting rights. According to him, INEC recognises that persons with disabilities have equal rights and that their votes, voices and contributions matter. He said the commission was implementing measures to remove barriers preventing PwDs from participating fully in elections. These include providing assistive materials, ensuring accessible polling units, training electoral officials and collaborating with disability organisations. Gajiram stressed that disability inclusion must be integrated into every electoral activity rather than treated as an additional responsibility. “Disability inclusion should not be treated as an additional responsibility but as an important part of our work,” he said. He urged Disability Desk Officers (DDOs) to maintain regular engagement with PwDs and communicate their challenges to the commission. He also encouraged participants to speak openly about their experiences and recommend improvements to electoral arrangements. “As we look forward to 2027, our goal is simple: to ensure that no eligible Nigerian is left out of the electoral process because of disability,” he said. He said INEC wanted wheelchair users to access polling units easily and visually impaired voters to receive appropriate assistance. Similarly, he said, persons with hearing impairments should have access to election information, enabling every eligible voter to participate with dignity and confidence. Also speaking, Gombe State Chairman of the Joint National Association of Persons with Disabilities (JONAPwD), Mallam Gambo Ahmad, commended INEC for organising the workshop. He described the arrangements as exceptional compared with previous engagements, particularly the provision of accessible communication materials. Ahmad specifically appreciated INEC for providing Braille materials for visually impaired participants and an interpreter for effective communication. He said the arrangements ensured participants could understand the discussions and contribute meaningfully to the proceedings. He identified intellectual disabilities, hearing impairments, physical disabilities, visual impairments, spinal cord injuries and leprosy-related disabilities among conditions represented in Gombe. item.title: Video: ‘Let Toluwanisings have a befitting burial’ – Woli Arole makes appeal
item.description: By Adegboyega Adeleye Comedian and preacher Woli Arole has appealed to those involved in the burial dispute surrounding late gospel singer Olayemi Bayonile Bolaji, popularly known as Toluwanisings, to allow him a befitting burial, urging them to end what he described as unnecessary public arguments. Arole made the appeal in a video shared on Instagram on Monday, describing the late singer as a great talent whose death had left friends and colleagues grieving. “I want to speak on behalf of Toluwanisings’ demise, and this is what God asked me to say. We’ve lost a great guy, a great gift to a generation. Even we, his friends and colleagues, have not recovered. For some of us, he is so close to us, and his death is really painful. A big elephant has gone,” he said. He also criticised people he accused of using the controversy to attract attention on social media, saying public discussion should instead focus on Toluwanisings’ wife and children. “It’s saddening and sad that a lot of people are now beginning to want to start to use it as a means for social media traction. You are m***. I have a right to say it. A young man had died in almost his prime, and the discussion is not even about the wife left behind and two kids? No. What you want to start doing is unlicensed, ungoverned, unnecessary talk, interviews and nonsense. A lot of people speaking about him this way never spoke about him while he was alive, about his music, please, please,” Arole said. He urged those involved to let the burial arrangements proceed and allow the singer to be laid to rest with dignity. “This is why it is a burden in my spirit, and I have to speak, and this is what the Lord is laying in my heart. The Bible says: Let the dead bury their dead. Whatever process, anything that needs to be done within that corner, let it be done. Let the young man be given a befitting burial,” he said. View this post on Instagram Woli Arole added that the burial dispute could not erase the singer’s musical legacy and called on the public to support his family and preserve his work through his children. “Nobody can ruin his legacy; he lived a good life, please. He sang songs that are eternal; his songs rang in our hearts. Whichever way he is buried, Toluwanisings is in our hearts forever; his sound is forever. So, please, I want to beg us in the name of Jesus, you should focus our energy on what is left: how his legacy will be preserved in his children and the wife,” he said. He concluded: “God bless Toluwanisings’ legacy, God bless his wife and his children, let the noise and unnecessary nonsense die down in the name of Jesus.” Toluwanisings’ family announced that the singer died in the early hours of October 14, 2026, but did not disclose the cause of death. The singer’s burial arrangements have drawn public attention following disagreements over where he should be laid to rest. item.title: US to exclude S. Africa, Rwanda from Africa duty-free trade deal
item.description: The United States Trade Representative on Monday said Washington would exclude South Africa and Rwanda from a major Africa-US duty-free trade deal, a blow to both economies, over practices “inconsistent” with the deal’s eligibility criteria. “These concerning and pervasive practices include, but are not limited to, barriers that undermine American trade and investment and practices that pose a threat to US national security and foreign policy interests in the region,” Jamieson Greer said in a statement. The exclusions will take effect from January 1, the statement said. The African Growth and Opportunity Act (AGOA), which grants eligible sub-Saharan African countries preferential access to the US market, has been renewed until the end of 2028, but is reviewed annually. South Africa is the program’s largest beneficiary but its eligibility has come under scrutiny as Washington steps up criticism of Pretoria, including false allegations of discrimination against white Afrikaners that South Africa rejects. On Thursday, South Africa’s trade minister said the country hoped for a favorable decision from Washington on the issue, arguing that continued market access would be in the best interest of both countries. A little over a week earlier, however, South African President Cyril Ramaphosa said the country should “prepare” for an adverse decision. The US president reviews countries’ eligibility for AGOA annually. Any removal requires 60 days’ notice to Congress and the country concerned. South African Trade Minister Parks Tau told reporters in Johannesburg last week that regardless of Trump’s decision on AGOA, his country’s economy would remain stable as it seeks other international markets. – Increasing pressure on Rwanda – Washington has been increasing economic pressure on Rwanda over its alleged backing of the armed M23 rebel group in neighboring Democratic Republic of Congo. Last week, the United States sanctioned the Rwandan defense ministry over those ties, which the Rwandan government denies. With Rwandan help, the M23 movement has seized swathes of the eastern DRC — home to valuable minerals coveted by world powers — since it took up arms again in 2021. Rwanda’s foreign minister told AFP last week that his country should not be a “scapegoat” for events in DR Congo. “The situation in the DRC, the political situation, the security situation, is mainly a Congolese issue,” Rwandan Foreign Minister Olivier Nduhungirehe told AFP on the sidelines of a Russia-Africa summit in Moscow before the US sanctions were imposed. “Rwanda must not be held as a scapegoat for what is happening in Congo forever,” he added. item.title: Nigerians, others to face 10-yr wait for UK permanent residency
item.description: United Kingdom, UK has revised its proposed immigration reforms, retaining plans to double the waiting period for most migrants seeking permanent settlement from five to 10 years while exempting hundreds of thousands of care workers from the extended requirement. The revised policy, announced on Monday, follows opposition from trade unions and members of the governing Labour Party over the potential impact of the changes on low-paid foreign workers, particularly those employed in the care sector. The British government had initially proposed last year that lower-skilled foreign workers should wait between 10 and 15 years before qualifying for permanent residency, officially known as indefinite leave to remain. However, under the revised arrangements, hundreds of thousands of care workers will be exempt from the longer waiting period, retaining a five-year route to settlement, subject to eligibility requirements. The exemption is significant for Nigerians working in Britain’s health and social care sector, which relies on foreign workers to fill staffing shortages. Despite the concessions, the reforms will still double the standard qualifying period for permanent settlement from five to 10 years. The changes, expected to take effect next year, will also apply retrospectively to migrants already living and working in Britain. Home Secretary Shabana Mahmood said the revised policy was designed to reward migrants who contribute to British society while imposing tougher conditions on those who violate immigration rules. “Those who contribute most will settle fastest,” Mahmood said. “Those who don’t play by the rules ‌will be refused or wait longer.” Under the new rules, migrants earning at least £50,271 annually and certain skilled public-sector workers will be eligible to apply for permanent settlement after five years, while those earning more than £125,000 can qualify after three years. Meanwhile, refugees who entered Britain illegally, particularly those who arrived by small boats, will face significantly longer waiting periods, potentially extending to decades. The government estimates that despite the exemptions, the reforms will reduce by 500,000 the number of migrants who arrived in Britain from 2021 and would otherwise have qualified for permanent settlement by 2030. As many as 1.4 million migrants are still expected to qualify within the same period under the revised arrangements. item.title: NUPRC opens bidding for 40 oil, gas blocks Nov 20
item.description: By Obas Esiedesa, Abuja The Nigerian Upstream Petroleum Regulatory Commission (NUPRC) has announced that bidding for 40 oil and gas blocks under its 2026 licensing round will commence on November 20. The Commission Chief Executive, Mrs Oritsemeyiwa Eyesan, disclosed this on Monday during a roundtable discussion at the 2026 ADIPEC Exhibition and Conference in Abu Dhabi. The discussion was titled, “Energy Sovereignty in an Interconnected World: Aligning National Priorities, Markets and Global Security.” In a statement by the Commission, Eyesan urged international investors to take advantage of opportunities in Nigeria’s oil and gas industry, saying improved security, attractive fiscal terms and incentives had made the country more competitive. She said the Commission would open its bid portal on November 20 and expressed optimism that the investment conditions would attract interested investors. “We are expecting investors to turn to Nigeria. We are going in for another licensing round and we will be launching our bid portal on November 20. We expect to see interested investors because the environment is a lot more competitive. “We have set a very attractive fiscal framework for investors. The entire environment is a lot more secure. We have been able to manage costs with a lot of incentives for investors and we expect to see investors take up the offer when we open the portal,” she said. Eyesan attributed the improvement in Nigeria’s investment climate to the Petroleum Industry Act (PIA), enacted in 2021, and executive orders signed by President Bola Tinubu. She said the Commission had conducted at least four successful licensing rounds between 2021 and 2026, attracting investments into the country’s oil and gas industry. According to her, the development marked a departure from the pre-PIA era, when licensing rounds were less frequent, adding that the reforms had strengthened Nigeria’s competitiveness in attracting upstream investments. On the country’s gas potential, Eyesan said Nigeria had an estimated 215 trillion cubic feet of gas reserves but was producing barely seven billion cubic feet per day, leaving significant opportunities for investors. She said recently completed and planned gas infrastructure projects would help unlock supplies, improve domestic availability and position Nigeria to serve regional and international markets. item.title: UNICROSS in turmoil as ASUU resumes strike after 104-day suspension
item.description: By Ike Uchechukwu, CALABAR The Academic Staff Union of Universities, ASUU, University of Cross River State (UNICROSS) chapter, on Monday, resumed its strike after 104 days, accusing the government of failing to honour agreements that ended the last one. The chapter Chairman, Dr Patrick Ushie, who disclosed this in an interview with Vanguard in Calabar, said the decision to resume the strike was taken at a union meeting today (Monday) following the government’s failure to honour agreements that led to the suspension of the industrial action on July 21, 2026. His words: “It is true that we have resumed the strike we initially called off on July 21 following a series of meetings with the government and its representatives. “However, certain agreements reached before the suspension have not been implemented as agreed by the government. “They have not only breached the timelines for implementation but have also failed to respond to our notices. “This time around, we are not going to suspend or call off the strike until our grievances are addressed,” he said. Recall that the UNICROSS chapter of ASUU embarked on an indefinite strike on May 19, 2026, over welfare concerns and the non-implementation of agreements reached with the union’s national body. The union had listed 11 demands as the basis for the industrial action, including the implementation of the salary structure and other welfare benefits of academic staff. Other demands included the immediate implementation of the non-financial components of the 2025 ASUU-Federal Government renegotiated agreement and increased government funding for the university. The union also demanded prompt payment of monthly salaries not later than the third day of each succeeding month. It further called for the payment of outstanding salaries and arrears of the 35 per cent and 25 per cent wage awards implemented in public universities since January 2023. The union also demanded the remittance of outstanding check-off dues owed to ASUU-UniCross and its national body since 2017, amounting to N11.9 million, as well as deductions for December 2024 and November 2025. Other outstanding demands included the payment of promotion arrears and earned academic allowances accrued between July 2011 and December 2017 under the 2009 Federal Government-ASUU agreement. item.title: NDDC denies bridge collapse report in Bayelsa
item.description: By Samuel Oyadongha, Yenagoa The Niger Delta Development Commission (NDDC) has dismissed reports circulating on social media that a bridge project under construction in Otuogori community, Ogbia Local Government Area of Bayelsa State, had collapsed. The Commission said an incident occurred at the construction site of the 600-metre Otuogori-Otuegwe Bridge, but insisted that the bridge itself had not been constructed and therefore could not have collapsed. Addressing journalists during an inspection of the project, the NDDC Director, Bayelsa State Office, Engr. Godknows Alamieyeseigha, described the reports as misleading. “We don’t have a bridge yet because we are still at the stage of crossing the beams. So, no bridge has collapsed. “However, there was an incident at the construction site, and we are assessing the circumstances surrounding what happened,” he said. Alamieyeseigha dismissed suggestions that the incident resulted from structural failure, describing it as an accident during construction. He expressed confidence that the construction company would address issues identified during the assessment and complete the project. He also said no bridge had collapsed in Bayelsa State or any of the nine Niger Delta states. The NDDC director said the Commission’s current board and management, led by Chairman Chiedu Ebie and Managing Director, Dr Samuel Ogbuku, had prioritised quality assurance in project execution. He added that NDDC engineers and independent consultants regularly inspected project sites across the region to ensure compliance with approved engineering designs and standards. Also speaking, the Managing Director of the construction firm, Mr Christian Emiezor, assured that the Otuogori-Otuegwe Bridge was being executed in line with high construction standards. He explained that the project was still at the preparatory stage, with work focused on positioning the beams before the construction of the main bridge structure. According to him, the incident occurred during the launching of the beams, which were being positioned on their bearings. “We are constructing a 600-metre bridge, but as you can see, we have not constructed a bridge yet. What you are seeing is just preparations for the bridge,” Emiezor said. He described the incident as a minor accident, explaining that a beam resting on a bearing but not yet secured could slide during the positioning process. “What was going on was the launching of the beams, and in the process, there was a slight accident. Because the beam was resting on a bearing and had not been secured, it could slide. That was what happened,” he said. Emiezor added that safety measures at the site prevented casualties. “The good thing is that, with the safety measures put in place, no life was lost,” he said. item.title: Hashim mobilisers take 2027 campaign to rural North-West
item.description: …Accord candidate’s supporters target six million votes across seven states Mobilisers for the Accord Party’s presidential candidate, Dr Gbenga Olawepo-Hashim, have extended their grassroots campaign to rural and underserved communities in Kano, Katsina, Kaduna and Jigawa states as part of a North-West mobilisation drive targeting six million votes. The campaign is moving beyond major towns and established political centres to engage residents of remote communities, including areas described by its organisers as ungoverned. The initiative is aimed at building a wider grassroots network across the states and taking Hashim’s message directly to communities often overlooked during conventional election campaigns. The rural outreach is part of a broader North-West mobilisation strategy announced by the Hashim Progressive Movement, which has set a target of six million votes across the region’s seven states: Kano, Katsina, Kaduna, Jigawa, Kebbi, Sokoto and Zamfara. The current phase focuses on Kano, Katsina and Kaduna, often grouped by the campaign’s supporters as the KKK states, alongside Jigawa. According to the organisers, the mobilisation is intended to expand political engagement in communities with limited government presence and inadequate public services. Previous campaign activities have included the appearance of Hashim’s posters in parts of Kano, Kaduna, Katsina and Jigawa, as well as engagements with support groups and political stakeholders. In Jigawa, the Accord senatorial candidate, Aminu Aminu, had expressed confidence in Hashim’s ability to challenge President Bola Tinubu in the state. The organisers said the rural campaign would also provide an opportunity to engage communities on issues including insecurity, agriculture, infrastructure, education, healthcare and access to economic opportunities. With the 2027 general elections approaching, the campaign said it intended to pursue its six-million-vote target through wider grassroots participation and engagement beyond established political networks and urban centres. item.title: Nigeria targets defence equipment self-sufficiency 61 years after DICON
item.description: ….DICON-D7G plans 7,000 jobs, seeks foreign investment, technology transfer By Ibrahim Hassan-Wuyo Nigeria’s drive towards self-sufficiency in military equipment production has received a boost, with DICON-D7G unveiling plans to expand indigenous defence manufacturing, attract foreign investment and create 7,000 jobs for retired military personnel and civilians. The initiative, being promoted at the ongoing Africa International Defence Exhibition (AFRIDEX) in Lagos, also includes plans to acquire about 40,000 square metres of land for an international defence exhibition centre. The Chief Executive Officer of DICON-D7G, Mr Osman Chennar, disclosed this in a statement issued to journalists on Monday, saying the initiative was aimed at reducing Nigeria’s dependence on imported military hardware through local production, technology transfer and industrial partnerships. DICON-D7G, a major sponsor of AFRIDEX, is using the exhibition to promote its vision of strengthening Nigeria’s military-industrial capacity through indigenous manufacturing, investment mobilisation and strategic partnerships. The initiative comes 61 years after the establishment of the Defence Industries Corporation of Nigeria (DICON) in 1964, as the country continues efforts to develop the capacity to manufacture a significant proportion of the equipment required by its armed forces. Chennar said the organisation was working to bring government institutions, private investors, local manufacturers, research organisations and international technology partners together to expand Nigeria’s defence manufacturing capacity. “Our ambition is to move Nigeria from dependence on imported military equipment to a country that can increasingly manufacture, maintain and sustain its own defence requirements,” he said. He said the objective went beyond importing finished defence products, stressing the need to develop local capabilities in the design, production, maintenance and eventual export of military equipment. According to him, Nigeria has the human resources, technical expertise and industrial potential to achieve greater defence independence through strategic investments and effective partnerships. As part of its international expansion drive, Chennar said DICON-D7G recently participated in an exhibition in Qatar, where it explored partnerships with foreign manufacturers, investors and technology companies to facilitate technology transfer and strengthen local production. He described AFRIDEX as an important platform for connecting manufacturers, investors, technology developers and other stakeholders. On the proposed exhibition centre, Chennar said the organisation was seeking approximately 40,000 square metres of land in Lagos for a facility that would host international defence exhibitions, technology showcases, industrial trade fairs and investment forums. item.title: NASS Considering Proposal To Create 74 Seats For Women, Says Bamidele
item.description: Leader of the Senate, Senator Opeyemi Bamidele, on Monday disclosed that the National Assembly Committee on the Review of the 1999 Constitution (as amended) had proposed the creation of 74 additional seats for women in the Senate and House of Representatives Bamidele, also Vice Chairman, Senate Committee on the Review of the 1999 Constitution, further revealed that the committee had proposed three additional seats in each State House of Assembly, all specifically reserved for women, without displacing any existing electoral seats. He made this disclosure at the 2026 Law Week organised by the International Federation of Women Lawyers (FIDA), Ekiti State Chapter on Monday, noting that the proposals were designed to deepen the inclusion of women in the country’s politics and governance process. A file photo of Senator Opeyemi Bamidele Ekiti FIDA, chaired by Mrs. Ayobami Olowoyo-Richards, organised the programme with the theme, “Justice in a Changing World: Responding to New Challenges Affecting Women and Children.” Bamidele attended the programme alongside the Chairman, House of Representatives Committee on Information and National Orientation, Steve Fatoba, and Speaker, Ekiti State House of Assembly, Adeoye Aribasoye, among others. “A Bill for an Act to alter the provisions of the Constitution of the Federal Republic of Nigeria, 1999 to provide for special seats for women in the National and State Houses of Assembly and for related matters is receiving our attention at the National Assembly,” Bamidele said. He further explained the centerpiece of the legislative initiative, which, according to him, was designed to create special seats for women at the National Assembly and State Houses of Assembly under the ongoing review of the 1999 Constitution. He added that the legislative initiative “is the fruit of extensive consultation and consensus-building. “It is why we commenced the constitutional amendment process early, ensuring that this is not a rushed, haphazard endeavour but a deliberate, inclusive, and thorough reform. “The proposal, as it stands, is meticulous in its design. It seeks to add 37 seats in the Senate and 37 seats in the House of Representatives. This suggests that if finally approved, each state of the federation, including FCT, will have one additional seat in each of the Houses of the National Assembly,” he added. Bamidele further revealed that the constitution review committee “has already proposed three additional seats for each state House of Assembly, all specifically reserved for women, without displacing any existing electoral seats. “This arrangement is proposed to run for a period of 16 years, four electoral cycles, before a comprehensive review.
